content:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty ALERT -> SLO breach detected: model=redwood-13b, route=/v1/generate, region=us-west-2. p95=1.3s (ok), p99=4.8s (>3s SLO). Streaming stalls observed. Trigger: 12:46 UTC. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/model-redwood-13b

alice.nguyen: I'm paged, starting triage. First check: are stalls concentrated on one node/pool?

bob_k: Looks like a single shared GPU pool (pool-gpu-shared-8) has high tail. p99 per-node: node-17 6.1s, node-21 5.9s, others normal.

eve-ops: Confirming noisy neighbor. IO wait on node-17 is spiking. iostat top: >80% util on nvme0n1.

charlie: Any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: model-variant redwood-13b-q4f2 -> node placement changed 12:10 UTC (deploy id: dpl-9812).

alice.nguyen: Noted. I/O spike lines up with that deploy. Could be tenant with heavy checkpointing or backup.

bob_k: Running quick checks. `ssh node-17` then `sudo iostat -xz 1 3` and `watch -n1 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv`

eve-ops: cgroups on node-17 show one container with high blkio. `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<cid>/blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes_recursive` shows large writes.

alice.nguyen: Who owns the noisy tenant? Metric tags show tenant_id=tenant-acme-corp, job=embedding-batch. Contacting CS. @dave_cs can you confirm?

dave_cs: Confirmed — acme-corp kicked off a large offline embeddings job earlier. They thought it would land in dedicated, ended up in shared. They're pausing now on request.

bob_k: Immediate mitigations: 1) throttle blkio for that container; 2) if still bad, cordon node and migrate affected model shards to other pool; 3) route traffic to fallback model-variant (redwood-13b-small) for latency-sensitive routes.

alice.nguyen: I'll apply blkio throttle to tenant container: `echo \"8:0 1048576\" | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<cid>/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device` (temporary).

eve-ops: Applied throttle. Monitoring I/O and p99.

bob_k: Also bumped cgroup cpu.shares down for container: `echo 512 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/docker/<cid>/cpu.shares`

alice.nguyen: After throttle: node-17 nvme utilization dropped to ~30% in 90s. p99 across pool now 2.1s (improvement), streaming stalls reduced but still some tails.

charlie: Good. What's customer impact? Which customers hit degraded latency?

dave_cs: Affected customers list: tenant-acme-corp (self-inflicted), tenant-beta-startup (external inference), a few free-tier apps routing through same model. Estimated 7% of production requests experienced p99 >3s during peak window. CS will reach out to top 3 impacted customers.

bob_k: Remaining tails look correlated with GPU context-switch spikes. Checking `nvidia-smi dmon` output and kernel logs. `dmesg | tail -n 200` shows multiple MIG allocation failures and some preemption events.

eve-ops: Node-21 also shows high cgroup memory.pressure. We should evict the batch job rather than keep throttling indefinitely. Suggest live-migrate that tenant to isolated dedicated pool or pause.

alice.nguyen: Agreed. Dave — please confirm acme-corp pause; if they can't, we'll move them to a reserved pool and bill for extra capacity.

dave_cs: They're pausing now. ETA 2 minutes.

alice.nguyen: Paused. Starting controlled drain of container and re-schedule to dedicated-reserved-1 (has capacity). Migration command: `rbctl migrate --tenant tenant-acme-corp --from pool-gpu-shared-8 --to dedicated-reserved-1 --graceful 30s`

bob_k: Migration started. Also enabling automatic eviction rule for future: set tenant_blkio_limit > 1GB/s per policy. Opening a quick policy override PR.

incidents-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress — throttle applied, migration started, p99 improving. Incident assigned to on-call alice.nguyen. Paging suppressed for next 30m.

charlie: Handing over to me for the next shift (12:46 -> 13:06 UTC on-call window). I'll monitor until migration completes. :thumbsup:

alice.nguyen: Handoff acknowledged. Notes: root cause = mis-scheduled heavy batch job into shared GPU pool; contributing factors = no blkio guardrail on shared pool + placement logic regression from recent deploy dpl-9812. Action list: - finish migration - add emergency throttle runbook - add placement guardrail (block large batch jobs landing on shared pools) - postmortem & customer comms draft.

bob_k: Will collect logs for postmortem: `journalctl --since \"-1h\" -u kubelet > /tmp/kubelet-node17.log`, `fio` tests queued for reproduction in staging.

charlie: Migration complete. p99 now 1.1s, streaming stalls resolved. I'll keep monitoring for 30m and then close incident if stable.

dave_cs: Sending interim customer note to impacted tenants.

incidents-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 13:20 UTC. Please file postmortem and link it here when ready.

charlie: Filing postmortem ticket: PM-INC-2026-1793456789. Assigning to infra and runtime teams.

alice.nguyen: Quick retrospective: need a pre-deploy canary on placement logic and enforce per-tenant IO limits on shared pools.

bob_k: Adding follow-ups: 1) implement blkio enforcement via cgroup v2 controllers; 2) tweak scheduler to prefer dedicated pools for large batch jobs; 3) add alert for nvme util >70% with tenant tag.

charlie: Thanks everyone. Closing thread after 1h observation if no regression. :white_check_mark:
